answer.label: Widely attributed to
answer.sourceLine: This saying is widely credited to Angela Davis, including on a UC Santa Cruz Arts Division page. That page gives no original occasion, and source researchers have documented earlier circulating versions without a Davis credit. Her exact authorship remains unconfirmed.

author.name: Angela Davis
author.heading: About Angela Davis
author.bio: Angela Y. Davis is a scholar and activist whose work connects feminism, racial justice and the prison system. A distinguished professor emerita at UC Santa Cruz, she helped found Critical Resistance and has written books including Women, Race, and Class and Are Prisons Obsolete?.

cite.sourceCitation: UC Santa Cruz Arts Division, “DEI Statement”; Barry Popik, “I’m no longer accepting…”, 19 July 2020; Norman Oder, attribution investigation, 20 July 2020.

copyAttribution: Widely attributed to Angela Davis; no original speech or publication established. Earlier unattributed versions are documented in source research.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The line reverses the familiar distinction between accepting limits and changing circumstances. Its circulation on banners and institutional statements fits Davis’s public association with social transformation, but neither that fit nor repeated credit establishes that she composed these exact sentences.

schema.claimReviewed: Angela Davis originated these exact words: I’m no longer accepting the things I cannot change. I’m changing the things I cannot accept.
schema.faqAnswer: The attribution is unconfirmed. Institutions repeat it with Angela Davis’s name, but no original Davis speech or publication is established here, and source research documents earlier circulating forms.
schema.verdictNote: Institutional repetition is not proof of origination; no alternative exact original author is established.
